pharm: Active metabolite albendazole sulfoxide binds parasite beta-tubulin, inhibiting microtubule polymerization and impairing glucose uptake, depleting parasite glycogen.
quick: >=60 kg: 400 mg twice daily; <60 kg: 15 mg/kg/day divided BID (max 800 mg/day)
Take with food (fatty meal increases absorption)
Avoid; embryotoxic/teratogenic in animals; pregnancy test first
CBC and LFTs every 2 weeks during therapy
summary: Albendazole is a benzimidazole anthelmintic indicated for parenchymal neurocysticercosis (Taenia solium larvae) and cystic hydatid disease (Echinococcus granulosus). Treatment requires monitoring of blood counts and liver enzymes, and a pregnancy test before use in women of reproductive potential.
indications: Parenchymal neurocysticercosis due to active lesions caused by larval Taenia solium (pork tapeworm)
Cystic hydatid disease of the liver, lung, and peritoneum caused by larval Echinococcus granulosus (dog tapeworm)

dosage.t: 28-day cycle, then 14-day drug-free interval, total 3 cycles

dosage.d: 15 mg/kg/day in divided doses twice daily with meals (max 800 mg/day)

dosage.n: Give steroids and anticonvulsants as needed

dosage.d: 15 mg/kg/day in divided doses twice daily with meals (max 800 mg/day)
dosage.n: Give steroids and anticonvulsants as needed

admin: Take with food (a fatty meal markedly increases absorption)
Tablets may be crushed or chewed and swallowed with water
Obtain a pregnancy test before prescribing to women of reproductive potential
For neurocysticercosis, give appropriate corticosteroid and anticonvulsant therapy
Consider oral/intra-cranial steroids to reduce inflammatory response in the first week
moa: Albendazole is converted to its active metabolite albendazole sulfoxide, which binds to parasite beta-tubulin and inhibits microtubule polymerization. This impairs the parasite's glucose uptake, depletes glycogen stores, and decreases ATP, leading to immobilization and death of susceptible helminths and larvae.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to benzimidazole compounds or any component of albendazole
monitor: Ophthalmic exam before retinal lesion treatment

preg: Avoid in pregnancy. Albendazole caused embryotoxicity and skeletal malformations in pregnant rats and rabbits at fractions of the human dose. Obtain a pregnancy test before therapy and advise effective contraception during and for 1 month after therapy.
lact: Limited human data; albendazole sulfoxide is excreted in low concentrations in animal milk. Weigh developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against maternal need.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment provided; experience in renal impairment is limited. Use with caution.
hepatic: Use with caution; hepatotoxicity and elevated liver enzymes can occur. Monitor LFTs before and during each cycle; discontinue if enzymes rise significantly.

moderate: CYP enzyme inducers may lower active metabolite levels
interactions.food: Take with food; a fatty meal increases oral bioavailability up to ~5-fold.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive hepatotoxicity risk.

serious: Bone marrow suppression (pancytopenia, agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia)

monitoring: CBC at start and every 2 weeks during each 28-day cycle
Liver enzymes before each cycle and every 2 weeks
Signs of raised intracranial pressure in neurocysticercosis
counsel: Take with food, especially a fatty meal
Tablets may be crushed or chewed
Use effective contraception during and 1 month after therapy
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bleeding/bruising, or jaundice
Attend scheduled blood and liver tests
Report severe headache, vomiting, or seizures
pearls: Poorly absorbed alone; a fatty meal increases absorption up to ~5-fold
Active moiety is albendazole sulfoxide, not parent drug
Monitor CBC and LFTs every 2 weeks; risk of marrow suppression and hepatotoxicity
For neurocysticercosis, co-administer steroids/anticonvulsants to control inflammation and seizures
missed: Take the missed dose with food as soon as remembered; if near the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Provide symptomatic and supportive care; consider gastric decontamination if recent. Monitor blood counts and liver function.
